title: World Cinema Radar — the podcast, Sunday 1 November 2026

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Hello, and welcome to World Cinema Radar, the podcast. I'm {A}, and it's Sunday the first of November. Welcome to a brand new month.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And I'm {B}. <chuckle> A new month, a new calendar. And since it's the first, we'll go through the whole of November later on.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: But first, the news. Seminci, the Valladolid film festival, has announced its winners. There was no gala this year, but there is a Golden Spike.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Then we have a look at Tokyo, where the competition is in its last days. One of the films there has already won a big prize in Spain.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: After that, a few series for November, including some horror, a giant box set of Game of Thrones, and a play you can see at the cinema, sort of.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Sort of is the key word. <short pause> All of it is in the written edition, with sources and dates. Let's go.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So, Seminci. The seventy-first edition of the Valladolid International Film Festival is over, and the Golden Spike goes to a film called Dao.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Dao. Directed by Alain Gomis. |Is that the French director?| Yes, French and Senegalese. And the film is a coproduction between France, Senegal and Guinea-Bissau.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That's right. The film moves between two celebrations, a wedding in France and a funeral rite in Guinea-Bissau. That's how it was described in the reports we read.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Lovely premise. And the Silver Spike?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That goes to La Gradiva, by Marine Atlan, a French and Italian film. It also won for best editing, and the Rainbow Spike, the LGBTQ prize.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Three prizes for one film. <chuckle> Not bad at all.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Now, individual awards. Best director is Lisandro Alonso, for La libertad doble. That's a coproduction between Chile, Argentina, Luxembourg, Germany and the United Kingdom.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Alonso is such a particular filmmaker. Slow, patient, very precise. And we'll come back to that film in a minute, because it's also in Tokyo.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Best actress is Alba Rohrwacher, for A Good Little Soldier, directed by Stéphane Brizé. And best actor is Swann Arlaud, for Un hombre de nuestro tiempo, by Emmanuel Marre.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Screenplay went to Sandra Wollner, for Everytime. And cinematography to Oliver Boonjing, for Notre Salut.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: There's also a special mention for Aquí, by Tiago Guedes. And the audience award went to Rose, by Markus Schleinzer.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: In the parallel sections, a few names. 9 Temples to Heaven, by Sompot Chidgasornpongse, won Punto de Encuentro. Alea Jacarandas, by Hassen Ferhani, won the history section. And the Spanish documentary prize went to Todo es cárcel, by Eloy Enciso.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The best Spanish director prize is Sebastián Uría, for Adiós, ríos. And the jury for the main section included Dennis Lim and Federico Veiroj.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Honestly, I like this list. It's international, it's not all big names. <short pause> But we haven't seen any of these films.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Right. A prize is not a guarantee that you'll like it. And we don't know yet which ones will get a commercial release in Spain.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The festival says that around a hundred thousand people came to the screenings. And the closing film, Gael García Bernal's Hombre al agua, plays tonight, even without the gala.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: One more thing about the context. The festival cancelled its closing gala out of respect for the victims of the rail accident in the province of Toledo. We told you about that yesterday.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: So the winners were published at an information event instead of a ceremony. It feels a bit strange for a festival that usually ends with such a big night.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Yes. But the screenings in Valladolid went on as planned. And there are also short film prizes. The Golden Spike for short films is Class Photo, by Arnas Balčiūnas, from Lithuania.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I like that the list has so many small films. <chuckle> Our listeners who love festival discoveries should keep an eye on Aquí and on Alea Jacarandas.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Let's be careful though. We haven't seen them, and we only know the official list. So we describe, we don't judge.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: So, Tokyo. The thirty-ninth Tokyo International Film Festival runs until the fourth of November, and the prize will be announced then.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: There are fifteen films in the main competition. And as you said, one of them is Lisandro Alonso's film. In Tokyo, it's called Double Freedom.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Same film, different title. <chuckle> It's a little confusing, but yes. La libertad doble in Spanish, Double Freedom in English.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Other names in competition: Bahman Ghobadi, with Trees Are Watching. Milcho Manchevski, from North Macedonia, with Sister Brother Manhole Cover.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I love that title. |Me too.| And Qiu Jiongjiong with Fuxi, Four Tales of Feasting, plus Garin Nugroho from Indonesia, and Yukiko Mishima from Japan.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Outside the competition, there are three big screenings. Sukiyaki, by Zeze Takahisa. Colony, by Yeon Sang-ho.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And Godzilla Minus Zero, by Takashi Yamazaki. That one opens in Spanish cinemas this coming Friday, the sixth.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Then the retrospectives. A big Kenji Mizoguchi series, with Ugetsu and Sansho the Bailiff. And eight films by Youssef Chahine.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: That's the kind of programme I'd travel for. <sigh> And there's a new film by Ulrike Ottinger, called The Blood Countess, with Isabelle Huppert.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: One note. This is a summary of the selection, not the full programme. And we don't have winners yet.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Let me add something about the title mix. Many of these films are coproductions between four, five or even six countries.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Yes. Sister Brother Manhole Cover lists North Macedonia, Bulgaria, Serbia, Albania, Italy and the UK. It's a very European way of making cinema.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And then Fuxi, Four Tales of Feasting, is a coproduction between Hong Kong, Taiwan, Japan, Saudi Arabia and Qatar. <laugh> It takes a spreadsheet to follow the funding.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: In the profile of our listeners, the interesting ones are probably the Asian titles and the history retrospectives.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Mizoguchi, in particular. Ugetsu is a ghost story, and Sansho the Bailiff is a historical drama. Both are about as close to the heart of period cinema as you can get.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: A thirteen-film retrospective, according to the report we read, although the list we saw had a few entries fewer, because one film is in two parts. So let's say around thirteen.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Sure. And please note, again, this is a selection and not the complete programme.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Now, series. We're using one guide here, from the Spanish newspaper Público, so the dates could change.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Start with the horror. Netflix has El cuerpo on the eleventh of November. Eight episodes, set in a Catholic school.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: A ritual goes wrong, and a group of students start having prophetic visions. That's all we know. We haven't watched it.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Catholic school horror. <chuckle> That's very much our territory.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The same day, the eleventh, Prime Video has season three of The Rings of Power. It jumps five years ahead.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And on the twenty-fifth, Blade Runner 2099. Eight episodes, with Hunter Schaffer and Michelle Yeoh. It's set fifty years after Blade Runner 2049, and all episodes arrive at once.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: A few more dates, quickly. The Altruists, on Netflix, the nineteenth. It's about the founders of FTX, with Julia Garner and Anthony Boyle.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And 12 12 12, on Apple TV on the thirteenth, a heist thriller with Anthony Mackie and Jamie Dornan. One episode per week.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The rest of the dates are in the written edition. Infamia and the Pazos crime we covered earlier this month.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Let me go back to The Rings of Power for a second. The third season takes place five years after the fall of Eregion.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So the story has jumped ahead. If you stopped watching after season two, that's worth knowing before you restart.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And Blade Runner 2099. All episodes at once on the twenty-fifth. So that's a weekend gone.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: <chuckle> Probably, yes. And for those who like sports and period dramas, remember The Greatest, the Muhammad Ali series, arrives on Prime Video on the fourth.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: We covered that one yesterday. It focuses on the early years, and it's the first scripted series fully authorised by Ali's estate, according to the sources.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: As for El cuerpo, the premise is the only thing we have. But it ticks a lot of boxes: school, religion, prophecies, group of teenagers.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Honestly? I'd give it a go. But we'll wait for reviews before we recommend it strongly. That's why it's only a three out of five, with low confidence.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Now something for collectors. Game of Thrones is getting a limited fifteenth anniversary box set on 4K, coming to Spain in November.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And it's huge. Thirty-three discs. Eight steelbooks, one per season, in a numbered metal case, with a booklet.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Over fifteen hours of extras. <gasp> Including a cast reunion filmed in Belfast, hosted by Conan O'Brien.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The picture is 4K, with HDR10 and Dolby Vision. English audio is in Dolby Atmos. But here's the catch.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Go on.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The Spanish audio is only Dolby Digital five point one. So if you watch it dubbed, you won't get the Atmos.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: That's a real detail. <short pause> And there's no price yet. The author of the article expects it to be expensive.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: It's one source, last updated in April. So we treat it as announced, not confirmed. Check the shops.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Who is this for? Mostly collectors. If you already own the earlier box sets, this one is about the steelbooks and the extras.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And the documentary, La última guardia. |Which is the one about the making of the series.| Yes, as far as we know.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: One more detail from the article. The distributor is named as HBO, although the author suggests Warner Bros may be the more accurate name.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Small detail, but it matters if you're searching for it in shops.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Now, theatre. We looked for complete recordings of plays and operas, and today we didn't find a new one with enough verified data.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: But there is something. National Theatre Live is showing Golden Boy, by Clifford Odets, at a cinema in Colchester, in the UK.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The dates are the fifth and the thirteenth of November. It's filmed at the Almeida Theatre, directed by Sam Yates, and it runs a hundred and ninety-five minutes.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And the cast includes Josh O'Connor, Daniel Mays and Hayley Squires. |Josh O'Connor? Again?| He keeps showing up. He was in the Bond screen tests we talked about on Friday.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: <chuckle> He really is everywhere. But here's the important part. This is a screening in a British cinema.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: So we can't say it's available from Spain. We don't know the recording date either, and the official site didn't show Spanish dates.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So no recommendation to watch it at home. Just a note. If you love British theatre, check your nearest cinema.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Let me say why we mention it at all. Odets is a classic of American theatre, and Josh O'Connor is a very interesting name right now.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And the Almeida is one of London's most respected stages. So it's a production worth watching, if you get the chance.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: But we have to be honest about what we know. We know the cast, the director, the dates in Colchester and the running time.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: We don't know the recording year, the language access in Spain, or any platform. So the report says that clearly.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And now the calendar. It's the first of the month, and it's Sunday, so we'll do the next seven days and then the month.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Wednesday the fourth: Tokyo ends. The Greatest, the Muhammad Ali series, arrives on Prime Video. And season two of All's Fair, on Disney Plus.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Friday the sixth is the big day in Spain. Godzilla Minus Zero, Sacamantecas, Los miserables, Ruega por nosotras, and a few more.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And on Netflix the same day, Possible Love, by Lee Chang-dong. Remember, that's the global date.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Then, next week. The eleventh: El cuerpo and The Rings of Power. The thirteenth: three Spanish cinema releases, Ti West's Scrooge film, Martin McDonagh's Wild Horse Nine, and Jaleos, by Isaki Lacuesta.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Also on the thirteenth, Infamia on HBO Max, 12 12 12 on Apple TV, and the Pazos crime on Netflix. Busy Friday.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The twentieth: the new Hunger Games film, and Jane Schoenbrun's Camp Miasma. A listing also includes Moulin, by László Nemes, but we couldn't confirm the Spanish date.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The twenty-fifth is Blade Runner 2099. The twenty-seventh: Hermanas, by Ione Hernández, and Sanguine.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Sanguine, the Sitges winner. But careful. One source says it opens on the twenty-seventh, another says the sixth.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So check it before you go. And on the thirtieth, the Gotham Awards ceremony. The dates from other countries, like Korea, Japan or the US, don't apply to Spain.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: One more thing about Friday the sixth. The listing also includes Fiesta Pagäna, by Álvaro Brechner, and El gato con sombrero.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes. And Godzilla Minus Zero opens in Spain on the sixth, which is the same day as the US. In Japan, it opens on the third.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Right. That's why we always separate the dates by country. A date from Japan or Korea doesn't tell you when it will arrive in Spain.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Also worth noting. Possible Love is listed for the sixth on Netflix globally. We haven't verified a Spanish cinema date.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And on Sunday the eighth, Ciudad de Dios, season two, on HBO Max. That date comes from a single guide, so keep it as provisional.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Our picks. First, Possible Love, by Lee Chang-dong, on Netflix from the sixth. Affinity four out of five, medium confidence.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Eight years after Burning. And it played in Venice. We haven't seen it, so that's based on reports.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Second, Sanguine, the French body horror about a young emergency-room resident whose body starts changing. It won at Sitges. Affinity four, medium confidence.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And a satirical look at work stress. <laugh> Which is relatable. Check the release date.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Third, El cuerpo, the school horror series. Affinity three, low confidence. And Golden Boy, also three, low confidence, because there's no verified access from Spain.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The week in review, quickly. A week of mourning and winners. Seminci closed without a gala, Sitges crowned Sanguine, and the Gotham nominations leaned towards auteur cinema.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And Clayface opened below expectations, while the Bond casting reached screen tests. Next week, Friday the sixth is the day.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Let me say a word about how we score. These numbers are editorial affinity with our profile, not critics' scores, and not audience scores.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Right. And the confidence tells you how much we really know. Low confidence means we only know the premise.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: So, our most solid pick is Possible Love, because of the director. And the one to watch the date on is Sanguine.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: So, the idea of the day. The prizes are in, and now it's time for the films to actually arrive.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And Friday the sixth is the date to circle. See you tomorrow on the Radar.
